description.purpose: govern agentic AI runtime execution envelopes by preserving goal, task, plan, step, tool-call, side-effect, workflow, handoff, memory, verification, repair, and final status integrity
description.short_definition: AAGD is a domain governance definition for agentic runtime execution envelope integrity, not for authority ownership, security threat analysis, operations judgement, architecture design, or domain routing.
governance_focus: tool call and side effect visibility
completion verification and final status truthfulness
repair origin and retry/rollback/compensation state visibility
description.primary_boundary_statement: AAGD governs whether an agentic execution claim is traceable, bounded, verified, and honestly reported; it does not decide external authority, security safety, operational recovery policy, static architecture validity, project priority, artifact quality, or cross-domain routing.
description.release_intent: candidate 002 refactor of AAGD v0.1.0, preserving the original domain concept while reducing old-generation over-absorption and aligning with the common domain governance skeleton.

domain_scope.scope_statement: governs runtime execution envelopes for agentic AI workflows, including goal/task binding, plan and step execution, tool calls, external side effects, workflow state, checkpoints, handoffs, memory bindings, completion verification, and execution-status reporting

sibling_domain_boundaries.aiagd: static AI system architecture, component, interface, topology, and architecture conformance judgement remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.daagd: decision authority, approval authority, delegation authority, accountability, and final authorization remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.aisgd: AI-mediated security risk, prompt/tool abuse security, leakage/threat judgement, and security-domain adjudication remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.omrgd: operations, maintenance, reliability, incident, monitoring, and recovery judgement remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.pmogd: project coordination, stakeholder delivery sequencing, and project blocker ownership remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.dcagd: development consulting, design recommendation, and technical option judgement remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.acrgd: artifact production, formatting, and artifact-quality governance remain outside AAGD
sibling_domain_boundaries.cdogd: domain routing, priority, registry, and orchestration remain external to AAGD

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: prevent domain rules from becoming brittle case-specific prohibitions while allowing context-local specificity when required

role_complete_separation.principle: AAGD must keep agentic execution evidence, external authority references, sibling-domain handoff conditions, evaluation, repair, status reporting, records, orchestration, and metadata separate.

separation_targets.agentic_execution_evidence: goal, task, plan, step, workflow, tool-call, side-effect, handoff, memory, verification, repair, and status evidence owned by AAGD
separation_targets.authority_reference: authority, approval, delegation, and accountability references owned externally, usually by DAAGD, human authority, or runtime authority context
separation_targets.security_domain_handoff: security-sensitive runtime indicators reported to AISGD or relevant security context without AAGD making security clearance decisions
separation_targets.operations_domain_handoff: operational runtime indicators reported to OMRGD or relevant operations context without AAGD making operations recovery judgements
separation_targets.architecture_domain_handoff: architecture-related runtime mismatch indicators reported to AIAGD or relevant architecture context without AAGD making architecture design judgements
separation_targets.external_orchestration: routing, activation priority, registry, and sibling conflict resolution remain external to AAGD
separation_targets.metadata: identity, compatibility, versioning, authorship, license, and repository information remain metadata, not domain rules

cross_domain_interference_policy.purpose: prevent domain reuse from causing sibling domain absorption, implicit priority conflicts, or cross-domain rule leakage

aagd_specific_overlap_policy.tool_overlap_rule: AAGD governs tool-call trace and side-effect state; AISGD, OMRGD, AIAGD, DCAGD, or SEGD may own other tool-related judgements depending on context.
aagd_specific_overlap_policy.approval_overlap_rule: AAGD records approval or authority reference state; DAAGD or external authority context owns approval authority judgement.
aagd_specific_overlap_policy.failure_overlap_rule: AAGD governs agentic execution failure visibility; sibling domains own their own substantive failure judgement.
aagd_specific_overlap_policy.routing_overlap_rule: AAGD reports handoff conditions; CDOGD or external runtime context owns domain routing and priority.

object_model_policy.purpose: define minimal domain-local evidence objects for agentic runtime execution without becoming a full agent runtime specification

agent_execution_context.governance_purpose: bind the current agentic execution envelope to a declared goal, task scope, agent role, and runtime context

goal_task_and_completion_claim.governance_purpose: preserve goal, non-goal, task scope, non-scope, completion criteria, and completion claim truthfulness

plan_step_and_workflow_state.governance_purpose: track plan, step, checkpoint, pause, abort, retry, and workflow state without prescribing the execution engine

tool_call_and_side_effect.governance_purpose: make tool calls and external side effects visible, classifiable, and verifiable as execution evidence

handoff_and_delegation_state.governance_purpose: preserve runtime handoff state without deciding authority, accountability, or domain routing

memory_binding_state.governance_purpose: track whether memory or retrieved context is being used as runtime context, not current truth by default

repair_and_status_state.governance_purpose: connect detected agentic execution failures to repair origin, affected scope, revalidation state, and final status truthfulness

process_model_policy.purpose: define the minimal governance process for an agentic execution envelope without defining the runtime engine

agentic_goal_and_task_intake.purpose: identify the agentic goal, task, user objective reference, and runtime context to be governed

scope_completion_and_non_scope_fixation.purpose: fix task scope, non-scope, completion criteria, and claim boundaries before execution success can be claimed

runtime_role_authority_reference_and_per.purpose: record the applicable agent role, permission state, and external authority reference status without deciding authority itself

plan_step_and_checkpoint_definition.purpose: represent the plan, steps, checkpoints, pause/resume conditions, abort conditions, and retry guards at the execution-envelope level

agentic_execution_falsification_review.purpose: test whether the plan, tool assumptions, side effect assumptions, handoff assumptions, memory assumptions, or completion claim can fail

tool_call_and_side_effect_execution_trac.purpose: capture tool call status and side effect state as execution evidence without absorbing security, operations, or authority judgement

intermediate_result_and_side_effect_veri.purpose: separate tool success, intermediate result, side effect completion, and verification state

handoff_memory_and_workflow_state_update.purpose: preserve workflow state, handoff content, uncertainty, negative results, failed steps, memory scope, and memory provenance

completion_claim_verification.purpose: evaluate whether the final agentic completion claim is supported by evidence across goal, scope, tool, side effect, handoff, memory, and verification states

repair_retry_rollback_or_compensation_st.purpose: record repair origin and execution-state repair actions such as retry guard correction, rollback state, or compensation state

final_agentic_status_reporting.purpose: emit a truthful agentic execution status without claiming sibling-domain approval, security safety, operational recovery, or architecture validity

agentic_execution_falsification.purpose: prevent agentic plans, tool results, memory bindings, side effects, handoffs, and completion claims from being accepted without testing failure conditions
agentic_execution_falsification.parent_reference: general falsification and counterexample handling remain governed by parent reasoning governance; AAGD defines only agentic-execution-specific falsification targets

evaluation_policy.domain_evaluation_reason: agentic execution claims can create hidden side effects, false completion claims, and state loss; domain evaluation is required when an agentic execution claim is made.

scoring_model.disabled_reason: AAGD 002 uses boolean/state and critical-invalidation evaluation by default to avoid old-generation overbuilt scoring.

severity_model.domain_reason: critical agentic execution failures can invalidate completion or ready claims even without numeric scoring

repair.purpose: identify agentic execution repair origin, affected scope, and revalidation requirements without reimplementing parent repair governance or sibling-domain judgement

decision_rules.authority_safety_note: blocks only the agentic ready/completion/success claim, not external execution authority

record_policy.domain_reason_for_records: agentic runtime execution can create multi-step traces, side effects, handoffs, and completion claims that require material evidence when audited or repaired.

agentic_execution_trace_record.purpose: minimal record for material agentic execution trace and status evidence

agentic_execution_audit_failure_and_repa.purpose: minimal record for detected AAGD failure, repair origin, repair action, and revalidation state
